title: For a flat morphism Gorensteinness at a point is equivalent to the shriek being invertible nearby
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter duality.tex (Duality for Schemes)

difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-shriek, for f : X -> Y a morphism of FTS_S and a point x at which f is flat, the lemma asserts the equivalence of f being Gorenstein at x and f^!O_Y being isomorphic to an invertible object in a neighbourhood of x, and that consequently the Gorenstein locus is open (statement lines 6721-6765). Setting omega = f^!O_Y, the proof notes that by Lemma labelled lemma-relative-dualizing-fibres it is a bounded complex with coherent cohomology whose derived restriction Lh^*omega to the fibre X_y is a dualizing complex, and it establishes a six step chain of equivalences: f Gorenstein at x; O_{X_y,x} Gorenstein; Lh^*omega invertible near x; Li^*Lh^*omega having exactly one nonzero cohomology of dimension one over kappa(x); L(h o i)^*omega having the same property, which is the same by Li^*Lh^* = L(h o i)^*; and finally omega invertible near x (proof lines 6723-6745). The first equivalence is the definition since f is flat, the second follows from Lemma labelled lemma-gorenstein, the third and fifth from More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-lift-bounded-pseudo-coherent-to-perfect, and the fourth is the composition identity (proof lines 6747-6765). Chaining the two directions through the pullback to the fibre and the point is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
